author: Astra research worker

quotes.quote:
The vhost sample application demonstrates integration of the Data Plane
Development Kit (DPDK) with the Linux* KVM hypervisor by implementing the
vhost-net offload API. The sample application performs simple packet
switching between virtual machines based on Media Access Control (MAC)
address or Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) tag. The splitting of Ethernet
traffic from an external switch is performed in hardware by the Virtual
Machine Device Queues (VMDQ) and Data Center Bridging (DCB) features of
the Intel® 82599 10 Gigabit Ethernet Controller.

Testing steps
-------------

This section shows the steps how to test a typical PVP case with this
dpdk-vhost sample, whereas packets are received from the physical NIC
port first and enqueued to the VM's Rx queue. Through the guest testpmd's
default forwarding mode (io forward), those packets will be put into
the Tx queue. The dpdk-vhost example, in turn, gets the packets and
puts back to the same physical NIC port.
quotes.claim: Actual service is VM packet switching; PVP test demonstration is not used to define mandatory copies.
Local destination MAC routes a packet to another vhost device RX queue; same-VM destination is dropped.
VM2VM_SOFTWARE local unicast branch returns before NIC queueing; selected workflow is VM-to-VM, not NIC ingress.
Guest posts its own receive mbuf address, length and WRITE flag; cookie associates descriptor ID with the same mbuf.
Used ID resolves to the original guest mbuf cookie; replacing a host pointer does not supply these bytes.
Real guest PMD obtains completion, validates minimum Ethernet length, removes virtio header from payload length, returns received mbuf, then refills.
Destination addresses come from guest descriptor chains, including noncontiguous/indirect layout handling.
Reserve advertised RX buffer capacity; no free descriptors means cannot accept; read/write permission for destination mapping.
Async segment copy maps guest addresses to backend host IOVA; enqueue and dequeue swap direction.
Full mbuf chain walks all payload pieces; CPU creates virtio header and DMA copies exact payload spans, including tails.
DMAdev copies all iovec segments; last segment marks packet completion and submissions are batched.
Acquire guest avail, reserve packet length plus header, keep src mbuf and descriptor count while DMA is inflight; rollback unsubmitted work.
Completed packet flags precede split used-ring release publication and notification; raw submission is not guest receipt.
Source host mbufs are reclaimed only after async poll completion; failed submissions handled separately.
Guest observes used index with acquire/read barrier before reading completed buffers.

quotes.quote:
**--dmas**
This parameter is used to specify the assigned DMA device of a vhost device.
Async vhost-user net driver will be used if --dmas is set. For example
--dmas [txd0@00:04.0,txd1@00:04.1,rxd0@00:04.2,rxd1@00:04.3] means use
DMA channel 00:04.0/00:04.2 for vhost device 0 enqueue/dequeue operation
and use DMA channel 00:04.1/00:04.3 for vhost device 1 enqueue/dequeue
operation. The index of the device corresponds to the socket file in order,
that means vhost device 0 is created through the first socket file, vhost
device 1 is created through the second socket file, and so on.

**--total-num-mbufs 0-N**
This parameter sets the number of mbufs to be allocated in mbuf pools,
the default value is 147456. This is can be used if launch of a port fails
due to shortage of mbufs.
quotes.claim: Two-device/four-channel deployment example supplies natural peer possibilities, not proof of simultaneous traffic or shared physical IOMMU.

quotes.quote:
Vhost asynchronous data path
----------------------------

Vhost asynchronous data path leverages DMA devices to offload memory
copies from the CPU and it is implemented in an asynchronous way. It
enables applications, like OVS, to save CPU cycles and hide memory copy
overhead, thus achieving higher throughput.

Vhost doesn't manage DMA devices and applications, like OVS, need to
manage and configure DMA devices. Applications need to tell vhost what
DMA devices to use in every data path function call. This design enables
the flexibility for applications to dynamically use DMA channels in
different function modules, not limited in vhost.

In addition, vhost supports M:N mapping between vrings and DMA virtual
channels. Specifically, one vring can use multiple different DMA channels
and one DMA channel can be shared by multiple vrings at the same time.
The reason of enabling one vring to use multiple DMA channels is that
it's possible that more than one dataplane threads enqueue packets to
the same vring with their own DMA virtual channels. Besides, the number
of DMA devices is limited. For the purpose of scaling, it's necessary to
support sharing DMA channels among vrings.

* Async enqueue API usage

  In async enqueue path, rte_vhost_poll_enqueue_completed() needs to be
  called in time to notify the guest of DMA copy completed packets.
  Moreover, calling rte_vhost_submit_enqueue_burst() all the time but
  not poll completed will cause the DMA ring to be full, which will
  result in packet loss eventually.

* Recommended IOVA mode in async datapath

  When DMA devices are bound to VFIO driver, VA mode is recommended.
  For PA mode, page by page mapping may exceed IOMMU's max capability,
  better to use 1G guest hugepage.

  For UIO driver or kernel driver, any VFIO related error messages
  can be ignored.
quotes.claim: M:N mapping permits multiple vrings to one DMA channel; large guest pages and timely completion polling are ordinary controls.

quotes.quote:
------------------------

* Memory pre-allocation

  For non-async data path guest memory pre-allocation is not a
  must but can help save memory. To do this we can add option
  ``-mem-prealloc`` when starting QEMU, or we can lock all memory at vhost
  side which will force memory to be allocated when it calls mmap
  (option --mlockall in ovs-dpdk is an example in hand).


  For async data path, we force the VM memory to be pre-allocated at vhost
  lib when mapping the guest memory; and also we need to lock the memory to
  prevent pages being swapped out to disk.

* Memory sharing

  Make sure ``share=on`` QEMU option is given. The vhost-user will not work with
  a QEMU instance without shared memory mapping.
quotes.claim: Async guest memory is preallocated and pinned; share=on allows backend mapping, not automatic cross-guest aliasing.
Source opens MEM_TO_MEM virtual DMA channel; not stream-only peripheral DMA.
DMA ring request is min(4096, device max descriptors), not a 4096-page task requirement.

quotes.claim: Source bounds: burst32, 256 descriptor vectors, 2048 async vectors; packet count/arrival are not fixed by these capacities.
Per-virtqueue async metadata scales with configured q and includes inflight packet metadata, completion flags and shadow used entries.
CPU memcpy path is a real built-in ordinary alternative and retains the same destination semantics.
External NIC RX is already per-vdev VMDQ; direct RX-to-guest must remain an ordinary alternative for ingress, so it is not the chosen necessary-copy argument.
Guest TX packets are dequeued then routed to another guest or physical port; source queue is an actual producer boundary.
Teardown drains in-flight asynchronous packets before reclamation.
Guest address becomes host_iova with finite contiguous range; host IOVA is distinct from guest virtual identity and does not prove physical IOMMU enablement.
Default mergeable/TSO/checksum feature choices can be retained without adding a compute consumer.
DEFAULT frontend directly exposes arbitrary address and byte-length registers; source and destination use one engine owner.
